# `sandloom.sdk.infra`

Infrastructure accessors, settings, the core runtime and (advanced) the facade.

Public API 1.0 (spec §2.2, Appendix C).

`from sandloom.sdk.infra import <name>`. Signatures in a terminal: `sandloom docs <name>`. Beginner names are the ones generated code and the examples use; any other name is advanced (mark its import line `# sandloom: advanced <reason>` in generated code and examples).

### `cache`

```python
def cache(name: str = 'default') -> Cache
```

Return the operation-based `CacheProvider` for a named instance.

The sanctioned cache surface for modules and core guards — `get`/`set`/
`add`/`delete`/`incr` (see
`sandloom.core.infra.contracts.CacheProvider`). Resolves via the
process-active `InfraRegistry` (`RuntimeError` when none is
bound); the registry's configuration picks the driver, so this surface
never names a concrete backend.

### `capability`

```python
def capability(ref: CapabilityRef[P], name: str = 'default') -> P
```

Return the instance `name` of the capability `ref` points to, typed by the
ref. A capability's package publishes the ref and the caller's Protocol, and the
capability's major version must match the ref's.

### `CapabilityRef`

```python
class CapabilityRef(Generic)(value: str) -> None
```

A typed key to a capability: `CapabilityRef[Search]("search.v1")`.

The caller's Protocol travels in the type, and a `.vN` suffix is checked against
the capability when it is resolved; a ref without one skips that check. A class
passed as `type[T]` cannot do this: mypy refuses an abstract class or a Protocol
there.

#### `CapabilityRef.name`

```python
name  (property)
```

#### `CapabilityRef.version`

```python
version  (property)
```

The `vN` suffix, if any. Only a versioned ref is checked on resolve.

### `ClaimsContributorContract`

```python
class ClaimsContributorContract(facade: CoreFacade, owner: str | None) -> None
```

`<module>.claims.v1` — a module's token-claims contributors as a contract.

Auto-registered for every module that adds a claims contributor; runs the
module's contributors (in its own read-only Unit of Work, like any read
contract) and returns their merged claims. A token issuer in another
process reaches it over internal RPC via `SERVICE_BINDINGS`.

#### `ClaimsContributorContract.contribute`

```python
async def contribute(self, user_id: Any) -> dict[str, Any]
```

Merged claims of this module's contributors for `user_id`.

### `core_from_request`

```python
def core_from_request(request: Request) -> CoreRuntime
```

SYNC accessor of the request's `CoreRuntime` (direct calls).

For code that holds a `Request` and cannot `await`: the same value as
`await get_core(request)`. As a dependency use `Depends(get_core)`
(async: no thread-pool hop), never `Depends(core_from_request)`.

### `CoreFacade`

```python
class CoreFacade(_ClaimsMixin, _RegistriesMixin)(
    app: FastAPI,
    settings_obj: Settings | None = None,
    service_registry: ServiceRegistry | None = None,
    get_db: Callable[[], Awaitable[AsyncSession]] | Callable[[], AsyncGenerator[AsyncSession, None]] | None = None,
) -> None
```

A module's strictly bounded access point to the framework's infrastructure.

Provides only methods that are safe and stable for modules to depend on;
concrete infrastructure details (cache backend, tracing implementation,
transport) stay hidden behind this API. One instance is created by the
composition root and handed to every module's `register(core)`.

#### `CoreFacade.event_bus`

```python
event_bus  (property)
```

Return the event bus owned by this facade.

The instance is bound via set_event_bus() during app wiring so each
application owns (and shuts down) exactly its own bus. Falls back to the
bare-facade in-memory bus for facades that never bind one (unit tests).

#### `CoreFacade.set_event_bus`

```python
def set_event_bus(self, bus: Any) -> None
```

Bind the event bus instance this application owns.

#### `CoreFacade.add_startup_task`

```python
def add_startup_task(
    self,
    task: StartupTask,
    *,
    critical: bool = False,
    phase: str | None = None,
) -> None
```

Register a startup task.

critical=True means the application MUST NOT start if the task fails:
run_startup re-raises instead of degrading silently.

`phase` is `"infra"` (runs first), `"modules"` (the default) or
`"post"` (runs last); a task's name never selects its phase.


#### `CoreFacade.module_registration`

```python
def module_registration(self, module_name: str) -> Iterator[ModuleAPI]
```

Scope a module registration so a failure leaves no partial state.

Yields a draft-backed `ModuleAPI`: everything the module
registers (routers, services, lifecycle hooks, health checks, event
schemas) is buffered in a `ModuleRegistrationDraft` and applied
atomically by `commit` only when `register()` returns normally. A
failure propagates without ever committing, so NOTHING is applied —
including event schemas, which the old snapshot/restore path left behind
as orphans in the contract inventory.

This replaces snapshotting private kernel state (`service_registry._map`,
`app.router.routes` slicing): the kernel is never mutated until commit.

#### `CoreFacade.increment_metric`

```python
def increment_metric(self, name: str, amount: int | float = 1) -> None
```

Atomically add `amount` to the counter `name`.

A real counter (monotonic, thread-safe): the in-process value
(`get_metric`) is updated under a lock and the increment is exported
to the Prometheus counter `sandloom_facade_counter_total{name=...}`. Use it
instead of a `get_metric`/`register_metric` read-modify-write.

### `CoreRuntime`

```python
class CoreRuntime(facade: CoreFacade) -> None
```

Read-only runtime view of the `CoreFacade` for module code.

Request-time module code (`Depends(get_core)`) gets THIS, not the full
facade: it can resolve contracts and capabilities, read settings, log,
trace, count, and collect token claims — but it cannot reach the event bus
(publish through `publish_event`), the infrastructure registry, the raw
FastAPI app, the service registry, or any `register_*` mutator.
Registration happens only through the
`sandloom.core.module_api.ModuleAPI` handed to `register(core)`.

This is an API-discipline boundary for trusted application code, not an
immutable object graph or a sandbox. Shared Settings must be treated as
read-only by modules; the remote-fact cache is maintained by shared authz
machinery. Do not mutate either from a business module.

### `get_core`

```python
async def get_core(request: Request) -> CoreRuntime
```

Return the read-only `CoreRuntime` view of the app's facade.

Module code gets contract/capability resolution, settings, logging,
tracing and counters — never the event bus, the infra registry, the raw
app or the `register_*` mutators (those belong to `register(core)`).

`async` on purpose: it does no I/O, and FastAPI runs a SYNC dependency in
the anyio thread pool on every request (a thread hop for an attribute
read). Use it as `Depends(get_core)`; a direct call is
`core = await get_core(request)`.

### `Notification`

```python
class Notification(
    channel: NotificationChannel,
    recipient: str,
    subject: str,
    body: str,
    data: Mapping[str, Any] = <factory>,
    dedupe_key: str | None = None,
    body_fields: Mapping[str, str] = <factory>,
) -> None
```

One outbound notification, independent of the delivery backend.

A logical message: which `channel` to deliver on, the `recipient`
address for that channel (an email, phone, device token, or user id for
`inapp`), a short `subject` and `body`, plus structured `data` and an
optional `dedupe_key` a driver may use to suppress duplicate sends.

`body_fields` are the values the `body` was built from, so a driver can
render its own template. They are as sensitive as the body (a secret link, a
name): a driver never logs them, and `data` stays safe to record.

### `notifier`

```python
def notifier(name: str = 'default') -> Notifier
```

Return the `NotifierProvider` for a named instance.

The sanctioned outbound-notification surface for modules: build a
`sandloom.core.infra.contracts.Notification` and `await
notifier().send(...)` — never import an email/SMS SDK. Resolves via the
process-active `InfraRegistry` (`RuntimeError` when none is
bound).
